speaker: Doctor
text: I have received your report of progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To determine the cause, could you tell me how long this has been going on and if you notice any redness or warmth in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a direct trauma event. Did the finger deform or feel unstable when it happened, and have you noticed any numbness or tingling in the ring and little fingers? REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_right_hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The X-ray confirms soft tissue swelling without fracture, which is concerning for a closed tendon injury. Do you have difficulty straightening the finger, and does the pain increase when you try to bend it?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hand_clinical_photo

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Ruptation). The patient's inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, combined with the finger resting in extension and the history of blunt trauma, confirms a rupture of the extensor tendon.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
